proposed.comparator_claim: Their bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion delivers honest weak-first-stage inference when the cutoff is known.
Their unknown-cutoff analysis obtains oracle substitution under a fixed discontinuity in a sharp-design treatment-effect problem.
Their ordered-modulus construction optimizes fixed-level expected length on convex fixed-index regression classes.
The paper studies nonparametric location estimation with a shrinking discontinuity under smoothness restrictions, but it does not validate the frozen fuzzy-RD moving-window profile.
Their multiscale work supplies scan architecture and exponential change-point control for step-function signals.
Their Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap theory supplies general stochastic maximal-control tools, but such control cannot repair the deterministic population-score misranking proved here.
Their Bayesian model propagates unknown-cutoff posterior uncertainty into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their working paper treats fuzzy regression discontinuity and unknown-discontinuity estimation in separate extensions.

prose_updates.tldr: The paper studies fixed-\(\alpha\) expected length of connected honest intervals for fuzzy-RD LATE when both the compliance jump and its unknown cutoff become statistically weak.  The finite-sample location-mixture converse proves a nonshrinking barrier below the signal-to-entropy boundary, and at \(s=1\) a total four-fold rectangular scan--refine--invert rule attains the known-cutoff order when \(n\kappa_n^3\) dominates \(\log(e/\kappa_n)\).  For \(s>1\), the frozen affine moving-window profile is now disproved as a uniform localizer by an explicit same-class sequence: its population score favors a displaced split even when \(T_n/\log(e/\kappa_n)\to\infty\).  The higher-smoothness detectable-region bracket remains open and requires a genuinely different estimator/profile or a negative frontier conclusion; the fixed-level critical-window law also remains open.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak fuzzy-RD inference and fixed-jump unknown-cutoff localization do not characterize honest connected LATE-interval length when the first-stage denominator and its location weaken jointly.  In the higher-smoothness problem, general stochastic maximal inequalities are insufficient because the frozen moving-window profile can be misranked already at the population level under separate one-sided smoothness.
project_justification.niche: The joint experiment combines a nonconvex union over cutoff locations, a causal outcome--treatment ratio, separate one-sided smoothness that permits a derivative kink, and fixed-level connected-length loss.  The counterexample shows that a locally affine compliance trend can make a displaced profile split fit better than the true split, a feature not resolved by point-estimation cutoff rates or empirical-process control alone.
project_justification.fill: The project fixes one observable-law class, proves the finite-sample location-mixture converse, and gives a total four-fold interval attaining known-cutoff order on the Lipschitz face.  For \(s>1\), it provides an exact projection counterexample to the frozen common-versus-piecewise affine profile and retains the bracket \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n+1/(n\kappa_n^3)\}\) as an explicit same-assumption OEQ requiring a new estimator/profile or a negative resolution.

prose_updates.related_work: Noack and Rothe (2024) motivate the observable class and known-cutoff bias-aware Anderson--Rubin inversion for weak fuzzy-RD designs.  Porter and Yu (2015) obtain unknown-cutoff oracle substitution under a fixed discontinuity in a sharp-design treatment-effect problem.  Frick, Munk, and Sieling (2014) motivate multiscale scan architecture, while Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2014) provide general stochastic maximal-control tools; neither prevents the deterministic population-score misranking exhibited by the higher-smoothness profile counterexample.  M{\"u}ller and Song (1997) and Tuvaandorj (2020) concern shrinking-jump or nonparametric location experiments, and no equation-level proposition from Tuvaandorj is used here.  Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018) supply an ordered-modulus and test-inversion template for convex fixed-index classes.  Madrid Padilla, Yu, Wang, and Rinaldo (2022) study aligned multivariate change channels without the monotone fuzzy-RD causal restrictions.  Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version) use a Bayesian unknown-cutoff fuzzy-RD model, and Arai, Otsu, and Seo (2026) discuss fuzzy and unknown-discontinuity extensions separately.  The proved frontier advance consists of the finite-sample converse and the Lipschitz oracle-attainment theorem; the new negative theorem rules out the frozen higher-smoothness profile localization route.  A replacement higher-smoothness procedure and the exact critical-window connected-length law remain open.
prose_updates.interpretation: At \(s=1\), the localization index \(n\kappa_n^3\) pays the logarithmic search cost, after which an independent fixed-center inversion has length \(n^{-1/3}/\kappa_n\), the known-cutoff order.  For \(s>1\), the frozen affine profile does not merely lack a completed concentration proof: a legal right-side affine compliance trend makes its exact population improvement larger at a split displaced by \(2H_n/5\) than at any split within \(H_n/8\) of the true cutoff.  This persists while signal dominates entropy, so a different population criterion or a negative frontier theorem is necessary.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The higher-smoothness profile branch remains a total measurable sample map, but it is not a valid uniform localizer on the stated class.  The counterexample satisfies every model condition, including the outcome-variance floor and correlation separation, and the exact projection polynomial has \(q(2/5)-q(0)=1111/46875>0\).  Uniform empirical deviations are smaller than this population gap on the exhibited high-signal sequence; on failed empirical-Gram samples the observable fallback is counted directly, and the maximizer comparison is made only when all Gram checks pass.  Thus stronger maximal-inequality constants cannot repair the frozen criterion.  This negative result does not rule out a genuinely different higher-smoothness estimator, prove the slope-kink converse, or determine the sharp critical-window law.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The Wald interpretation, known-cutoff benchmark, finite-sample location-mixture barrier, and Lipschitz-face oracle attainment retain their full stated scope.  For \(s>1\), the paper proves only that the frozen common-versus-piecewise moving-window profile fails the proposed uniform localization inequality on the unchanged class; it does not conclude that every estimator fails or that the candidate detectable-region bracket is false.  That bracket remains an OEQ requiring a genuinely different estimator/profile or a negative frontier conclusion.  No cross-side derivative matching, latent-cell H{\"o}lder restriction, adaptation guarantee, disconnected-set result, or matched critical-window constant is added.
